;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]], [[Egypt–Libya relations]]
**In a closed-door session, the [[Parliament of Egypt]] authorizes the [[Egyptian Armed Forces|military]] to intervene in neighbouring [[Libya]]. [[President of Egypt|President]] [[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] has said [[Sirte]] is a "red-line", and that any attack on the strategic Libyan city would prompt Egyptian military action. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/egypts-lawmakers-vote-deploying-troops-libya-71873091 (ABC News)]
*[[Israeli involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Syrian Air Defense Force|Syrian air defenses]] respond to a strike over [[Damascus]] attributed to [[Israel]], state media reports, in the latest wave of attacks that Western intelligence sources have said were Israeli strikes on a major [[Iranian involvement in the Syrian Civil War|Iranian-backed]] ammunition depot on the edge of the capital. According to a Syrian military sources, at least seven soldiers were wounded in the attack which also inflicted "heavy material damage". [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/syria/.premium-israeli-strikes-target-iranian-backed-militias-near-damascus-report-says-1.9008241 (''Haaretz'')]

;Arts and culture 
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema]]
**[[Cinema of China]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Shanghai]]
***Cinemas in [[Shanghai]] and [[Chengdu]] reopen after a six-month closure. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-china-cinemas/cinemas-in-china-begin-to-reopen-after-six-month-coronavirus-closure-idUSKCN24L147 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Popular music]] magazine ''[[Q (magazine)|Q]]'' announces it is ceasing operations after 34 years in print amid an accelerated downturn in sales due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-bauer-media-group/uk-music-magazine-q-to-close-after-34-years-hurt-by-coronavirus-pandemic-idUKKCN24L2OX?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Ministry of Citizenship (Brazil)|Citizenship Minister]] [[Onyx Lorenzoni]] and [[Ministry of Education (Brazil)|Education Minister]] [[Milton Ribeiro]] test positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-brazil-idUSKCN24L235 (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[European Union|EU]] meeting on a post-[[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|coronavirus]] recovery fund enters deadlock on its fourth day. Complicating matters, the group is also negotiating a deal for the bloc's next long-term budget. Today's early talks over a proposed [[euro|€]]750bn ([[United States dollar|$]]857bn / [[pound sterling|£]]680bn) recovery package have reportedly been testy. Resumption is scheduled for 14:00 [[GMT]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53468554 (BBC News)]
*[[China–United Kingdom relations]], [[Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[Foreign and Commonwealth Office|UK Foreign Minister]] [[Dominic Raab]] announces that the [[United Kingdom]] will "immediately and indefinitely" suspend its extradition treaty with [[Hong Kong]] over the [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|controversial national security law]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-53476811 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[List of George Floyd protests in the United States|George Floyd protests in the United States]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Chicago]]
***Mayor [[Lori Lightfoot]] says she has "great concerns" about the possibility that [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] could deploy federal agents to [[Chicago]] to crack down on [[Gun violence in the United States|gun violence]] and protests, similar to an approach in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]], [[Oregon]]. The Trump Administration will be sending 175 federal agents to Chicago to assist police in curbing violent crime. [https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2020/07/20/mayor-lori-lightfoot-concerned-about-trump-possibly-deploying-federal-agents-in-chicago-thats-not-what-we-need/ (WBBM-TV)]
*[[Capital punishment in Iran]]
**Iranian [[Mahmoud Mousavi-Majd]], convicted of [[spying]] for the [[United States]] and Israel and on the [[Revolutionary Guards]] commander, [[Qasem Soleimani]], is executed by hanging in [[Iran]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53470950 (BBC News)]
*Police in [[Panama]] arrest a person linked to a [[mass shooting]] two days ago which resulted in six young people killed with gunshot wounds to the head. Investigators suspect that it was a targeted attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-53467067 (BBC News)]
*[[Roy Den Hollander]], a self-described [[Antifeminism|antifeminist]] [[lawyer]], is named as the attacker behind the shooting at the home of [[United States federal judge|U.S. District Judge]] [[Esther Salas]] last night, which left her son dead and her husband critically injured. Den Hollander has been found dead at a home in [[Rockland, New York]], and is also being investigated in connection to the earlier shooting death of a [[southern California]] lawyer. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/07/20/esther-salas-mark-anderl-shooting-new-jersey-home/5470802002/ (''USA Today'')] [https://www.thedailybeast.com/gunman-ambushes-nj-federal-judge-esther-salas-husband-mark-anderl-and-son-at-home (''The Daily Beast'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/suspect-shooting-death-federal-judge-s-son-found-dead-believed-n1234365 (NBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Georgia]]
**[[Democratic Party of Georgia]] Chair and [[Georgia State Senate|State Senator]] [[Nikema Williams]] is selected by the party's Executive Committee to replace the name of the late incumbent [[John Lewis (civil rights activist)|John Lewis]] on the ballot for [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]'s [[Georgia's 5th congressional district|5th congressional district]] for the November 3 general election. [https://www.ajc.com/politics/politics-blog/democrats-tap-nikema-williams-to-replace-john-lewis-on-november-ballot/KM475QUFGRBMXMHCHWJN56SNMA/ (''Atlanta Journal-Constitution'')]
*[[King of Saudi Arabia|King]] [[Salman of Saudi Arabia|Salman]] of [[Saudi Arabia]], 84, is admitted to a hospital due to an inflammation of the [[gall bladder]]. The hospitalization prompts [[Iraqi Prime Minister]] [[Mustafa Al-Kadhimi]] to cancel his scheduled visit to Saudi Arabia. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-politics-king/saudi-king-salman-84-admitted-to-hospital-idUSKCN24L055 (Reuters)]
